blocks.text: When two bodies travelling along an axis do not end up traveling along the same initial axis after collision, then it is a case of two-dimensional collision. When the collision is elastic, the system of bodies conserves both its total linear momentum and total kinetic energy.

blocks.alt: x and y axes with ball m₂ at rest at the origin. Ball m₁ comes from the left with velocity v₁ᵢ along the x-axis. After the collision m₂ moves off above the x-axis at angle θ₂ with velocity v₂f, and m₁ moves off below the x-axis at angle θ₁ with velocity v₁f.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.15: Elastic collision in two dimensions (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.15).

blocks.text: Consider two bodies colliding elastically at a certain glancing angle, showing that the collision is not head-on. Let m₁ be the mass of the first body (projectile) moving with initial velocity v⃗₁i and m₂ is the mass of the body second (target), which is initially at rest, v⃗₂i = 0. As the two bodies collide together, the impulses generated between them, send these bodies off at angles θ₁ and θ₂ to the x-axis, along which the projectile initially travelled.
An elastic collision that is not a head-on collision between two bodies.
Initially, the body with mass m₂ (target), is at rest.
